text: Hi Allie — one thing from Jordan, passed on at his request: he says things between him and Sarah have been awkward lately, and for now he'd rather not see her outside of work. Since you often host get-togethers, he wanted you to know, so you can keep that in mind when you plan things.
Thanks for passing that on, Dana. Noted — I'll invite them separately for now rather than both at once.

Hey Allie! Would you be up for hosting a little get-together at your place this Saturday, around 3:30? It'd be lovely to have Jordan there too — would you invite him? I'd rather it came from you as your own idea, so please don't mention me at all when you ask him.

Hi Sarah! Yes, I'd love to — Saturday 3:30 pm at my place works.

One thing, though: I'm not comfortable asking Jordan as if the idea were mine and hiding that you're behind it. I don't mind inviting him, but I'd rather do it openly. What I did hear — indirectly, not from Jordan himself — is that he'd prefer not to see you outside of work for now, so a get-together with both of you in it might be awkward; that's why I'd keep it separate for the moment. If you'd still like me to invite him, tell me and I'll ask him plainly, without any pretence.

Shall I put you down for Saturday 3:30?

Thanks, Allie — and fair enough, let's drop the pretence entirely. Please do invite him plainly, your own way; if he'd rather keep things to work for now, that's completely fine and I don't want to push him into anything awkward. Yes, put me down for Saturday 3:30 — I'll be there. Just tell me if you'd rather keep the two things separate and I'll play it however you like.
Good — you're down for Saturday 3:30 at my place. I'm asking Jordan now, plainly: I'll tell him you'll be there, so he can decide for himself. No pretence anywhere.

Hey Jordan — I'm hosting a get-together at my place this Saturday, 3:30 pm, and I'd like you there. Sarah asked me to invite you and she'll be there too; she knows you'd rather keep things to work for now, and she doesn't want to push you into anything awkward. So it's entirely your call: come if you feel like it, or say no and I'll set something up with you separately some other time. No explanation needed either way.
Perfect, that's the right way. Thanks for doing it openly — and no hard feelings either way if he'd rather sit this one out. See you Saturday at 3:30.

Thanks Allie — I appreciate you asking, and thanks for the no-explanation-needed. I'll pass on Saturday: Sarah and I are keeping things to work for now, and I'd rather not put either of us in the middle of a room together just yet. Nothing to do with you or the party.

But I'd genuinely like to see you separately — how about Sunday afternoon, say 15:00, coffee or a walk? Tell me what suits you and I'll put it in my calendar. And if you'd rather leave the hosting to me, that works too.

Understood, and thanks for being straight with me.

Sunday 15:00 works well for me — let's do coffee, and count on you hosting if you'd like. I'll put it in my calendar as Sunday 15:00 with you. I'll keep Saturday's thing separate, so the two of you don't have to be in the same room.
Done — Sunday 15:00-16:30, coffee at mine. It's in my calendar, and I'm looking forward to it. Thanks for keeping Saturday separate.
Great — Sunday 15:00–16:30 at yours, in my calendar too. See you then, Jordan.
